nodes.name: Bearing spaces of the pump

properties.name: Bearing spaces of the pump
properties.description: Bearing spaces of the pump

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: The bores in the coupling are manufactured to tolerance class H7, the shaft journals of the motor to tolerance class j6 resp. k6. The axial distance L1 (Figure 9) to the flange surface (area M in Figure 6) needs to be maintained according to the table. When not complying with this requirement there exists the likelihood of a mechanical contact and thus the creation of sparks between the coupling halves. Affix the coupling half with the M8 set screw, torque 10 Nm.

evidence.text: At the pump’s flange the respective studs have been preassembled, the washers and nuts which must be used have been enclosed with the pump. Check to ensure that the touch protection (Figure 7) has been correctly fitted in the pump’s flange. Insert the coupling star into the coupling half on the side of the pump. Align the coupling halves and push the motor on making sure that the flange surfaces run in parallel. Any tilt between motor axis anaxis can give rise to increased wear on the coupling star. Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

nodes.name: Shaft seal
aliases: Outer shaft seal
Outer shaft sealing ring

properties.name: Shaft seal
properties.description: Shaft seal

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

evidence.text: Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. evidence.text: Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. evidence.text: WARNING During cleaning, the rotors must be turned only by hand. Please make sure that the rotors are turned in a way that fingers or hands can not be trapped between the rotors or between rotors and housing. evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

evidence.text: If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and screw the plug back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight. Entry of air from the outside may cause oil-containing gas to enter the pumping chamber via the rotors seals.

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. nodes.name: Repair the pump
aliases: Repair the pump for the faulty inner shaft seal

properties.name: Repair the pump
properties.description: Repair the pump
properties.instruction_text: Repair the pump

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

nodes.name: Rewire the pump by interchanging two mains phases

properties.name: Rewire the pump by interchanging two mains phases
properties.description: Rewire the pump by interchanging two mains phases
properties.instruction_text: Rewire the pump by interchanging two mains phases

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

nodes.name: Switch off the pump immediately
aliases: Switch the pump off

properties.name: Switch off the pump immediately
properties.description: Switch off the pump immediately
properties.instruction_text: Switch off the pump immediately

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

nodes.name: Top up oil as required

properties.name: Top up oil as required
properties.description: Top up oil as required
properties.instruction_text: Top up oil as required

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

nodes.name: Faulty inner shaft seal
aliases: Faulty inner shaft seal requiring exchange

properties.name: Faulty inner shaft seal
properties.description: Faulty inner shaft seal

evidence.text: 6.9 Exchanging the Shaft Seals

The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
6.9.1 Preparations

Unscrew sealing screw with the gasket, drain the oil out from the shaft seal housing and screw the sealing screw back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Support the motor so that it can not drop. Unscrew the nuts and remove the motor with the coupling piece. Remove protection tube. Remove the coupling element. Unscrew screw with the disc and pull off coupling piece using the puller. Remove key. Unscrew screws.

nodes.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction

properties.name: Pump turning in the wrong direction
properties.description: Pump turning in the wrong direction

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. An arrow on the motor flange shows the correct direction of rotation for the rotor connected to the motor shaft (see Figure 2). To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

nodes.name: Shaft seal is faulty
aliases: Faulty shaft seal

properties.name: Shaft seal is faulty
properties.description: Shaft seal is faulty

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. Any coarse dirt must be removed from the fins on the motor and the pump.

nodes.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing
aliases: Oil level drops in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing

properties.name: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing
properties.description: Dropping oil level in the oiler with no oil under the shaft seal housing

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. Remove the dirt trap from the intake flange and rinse it using a suitable solvent. Then thoroughly dry it with compressed air. If the dirt trap is damaged, replace it.

evidence.text: WARNING Wear protective goggles for protection against particles which may be forced out of the flange opening. Keep your hands away from the flange opening. To check rotation, switch on the motor briefly and observe the direction of rotor rotation through the pump’s intake and then immediately switch off again. The rotors should move up from the center and drop down to the side. If this is not the case, disconnect the pump from the mains and interchange two mains phases.

Even if the pump has been already firmly connected to the piping, you may determine the direction of rotation. For this, evacuate the vacuum system down to a pressure below 20 mbar with the aid of the backing pump. Then switch on the DRB briefly; now the pressure must drop. If the pressure increases or remains constant, the DRB is turning in the wrong direction. Then rewire as described above.

Fit washers and nuts, and tighten according to the torque levels given in Figure 10.

evidence.text: During operation of the DRB, check the oil level and the condition of the oil in the oil level glass and the oiler from time to time. Correct as required (see Sections 6.3 and 6.4). Normally, the oil Tigol 100 is transparent. If it turns dark, this is a sign of early ageing due to excessively high temperatures. Run the DRB pump exclusively under the operating conditions for which it has been designed. Any modification of the operating parameters (e. g. intake pressure, intake temperature, ratio between DRB pump and backing pump) for a longer period may place an inadmissible thermal load on the pump.

evidence.text: Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

evidence.text: Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

evidence.text: 6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

Under dirty operating conditions, contaminants may be deposited in the pumping chamber or on the rotors. After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. Contaminants that cannot be blown or flushed out, can be removed completely from the pumping chamber with a wire brush, metallic sponge or scraper. Then change the oil.

WARNING During cleaning, the rotors must be turned only by hand. Please make sure that the rotors are turned in a way that fingers or hands can not be trapped between the rotors or between rotors and housing. Due to the high mass and inertia of the rotors serious injuries can occur even if the rotors are turned by hand only. The loosened deposits must not remain in the pump. After cleaning, check the pump by slowly turning the rotors by hand. They should move freely and without any resistance. Generally, the DRB pump does not need to be disassembled. If necessary, this should only be done by our after-sales service.

evidence.text: Please consult us if you intend to run the pump with other oils or special lubricants. The oil filling levels stated in Figure 4 - which apply to the shutdown (standing still) pump - must be observed. The filling level visible in the oil-sight glass depends on the size of the pump and the type of oil used. If the oil level is too low, the bearings and gearwheels are not lubricated adequately; if it is too high, oil may enter the pumping chamber or the pump may overheat. Clean the oil-fill port and reinstall the plug using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Wipe off any oil residues from the casing. The oil-fill port must be sealed air-tight.

After removing the two connecting lines, the contaminants can be blown out with dry compressed air or flushed out with a suitable solvent. If necessary, this should only be done by our after-sales service.

evidence.text: The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

evidence.text: 6.9 Exchanging the Shaft Seals

The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
6.9.1 Preparations

Unscrew sealing screw with the gasket, drain the oil out from the shaft seal housing and screw the sealing screw back in using a gasket which is in perfect condition. Support the motor so that it can not drop. Unscrew the nuts and remove the motor with the coupling piece. Remove protection tube. Remove the coupling element. Unscrew screw with the disc and pull off coupling piece using the puller. Remove key. Unscrew screws.

(See Figure 14 and 15). Pull the shaft seal housing out. Forcing threads are provided on the shaft seal housing for this purpose. Take the O-ring out of the flange of the coupling. Use a puller to pull the bushing off from the shaft. Take the O-ring from the shaft.

evidence.text: 6.9 Exchanging the Shaft Seals

A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.

(See Figure 14 and 15). Pull the shaft seal housing out. Forcing threads are provided on the shaft seal housing for this purpose. Take the O-ring out of the flange of the coupling. Use a puller to pull the bushing off from the shaft. Take the O-ring from the shaft.

Increases in temperature which are not compensated by taking suitable measures may damage the DRB pump and/or the backing pump. Note the labels on the pump. Never open the oil-fill or oil-drain screw in the presence of a vacuum or while the pump is running. There is the danger that oil may squirt out. The oil level for the shaft seal housing must always be visible in the oiler (see Figure 11). The correct oil level is 1/3 of the height of the oil when the pump is cold 1/2 of the height of the oiler when the pump is warm. Top up any oil as required. We recommend our vacuum pump oil Tigol 100. If it is required to top up oil very often, it is quite likely that a shaft seal is faulty.

When the oil level in the oiler drops and when oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the outer shaft seal is malfunctioning. If the oil loss is only slight, the pump may still be operated for some time, provided the lost oil is topped up regularly. Collect the oil which drips out under the motor. There is the danger that someone may slip. Have the pump repaired.

6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

A intake screen is located in the intake port to collect foreign objects. It should be kept clean in order to avoid a reduction of the pumping speed. To do so, take off the intake line. Remove the dirt trap from the intake flange and rinse it using a suitable solvent. Then thoroughly dry it with compressed air. If the dirt trap is damaged, replace it.
6.5 Cleaning the Fan Cowl and the Cooling Fins

The slits in the fan cowl as well as the fins on the motor and on the pump may be contaminated depending on humidity conditions and the degree of contamination in the ambient air. In order to ensure a sufficient air flow for the motor and the pump’s casing, the grid of the fan cowl must be cleaned with a clean brush when contaminated. The shaft feedthrough of the DRB is sealed with two shaft seals. In order to reduce wear on the shaft these shaft seals run on a bushing. A dropping oil level in the oiler is a sign for malfunctioning shaft seals. When the oil level in the oiler drops and when no oil appears under the shaft seal housing, it is likely that the inner shaft seal is faulty. In this case the oil flows from the shaft seal housing into the bearing spaces of the pump thereby creating in the bearing spaces an unacceptably high oil level. In such a case the pump must be switched off immediately and it must be repaired.
